Specifically, Ganoderic Acid K is linked to Serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 2A catalytic subunit beta isoform, which is a known target of several compounds, including 1-[3-methoxy-4-[(3R,4S,5S,6R)-3,4,5-trihydroxy-6-(hydroxymethyl)oxan-2-yl]oxyphenyl]ethanone, 4-Chloro-3,5-Dihydroxytoluene, and 5-N-Tricosylresorcinol. These compounds all have a shared mechanism of action, targeting Gamma-secretase through a common pathway involving the serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 2A catalytic subunit beta isoform. The consistent presence of this intermediate in multiple pathways supports the hypothesis that Ganoderic Acid K may interact with Gamma-secretase through a similar mechanism, possibly by modulating the activity of the phosphatase subunit. The evidence is robust and consistent across different compounds, suggesting a plausible biological relationship. However, the exact nature of the interaction remains uncertain, and further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of Ganoderic Acid K in the regulation of Gamma-secretase.
